correctness.rationale: An all-length necessary quotient test is derived from palindrome reversal and real interval normalization; the finite 14-bit arithmetic certificate checks all t,b and a intervals exactly, counts 45362298 forbidden cylinders, and minimizes all 8193 prefix boundary ratios at 80469557/240599040. Integer arithmetic of verify.cpp has checked range bounds, direct independently implemented small-width tests agree, and a finite set of short denominators contributes only O(sqrt X). The density calculation includes all dyadic partial shells and all even integers; the resulting upper bound is 39829963/240599040.

originality.rationale: Bai et al. (2022), §2.4 Theorem 8/Corollary 9/Remark 10, certify a three-bit obstruction (lower-density 1/40 for their odd excluded subclass) and suggest stronger bounds; §2.2 supplies an individual membership algorithm; Conjecture 2 asks density zero. The new uniform bound upper density below 1/6 is not stated or implied by those results. A previously established three-bit two-cylinder calculation gives the weaker complement lower bound 11/20 and does not imply the width-14 estimate. Targeted external searches and semantic mathematical-result searches found no equivalent or broader quantitative bound. Unindexed equivalent work remains possible.

value.rationale: The upper-density estimate falls strictly below the natural one-sixth threshold (equivalently more than five-sixths of integers are excluded), a substantial strengthening of the published three-bit single-cylinder 1/40 odd exclusion and earlier 11/20 complement bound. It addresses the quantitative problem underlying the published conjecture that the quotient set has density zero, with a reusable exact k-bit obstruction framework and complete finite cutoff at width 14; not a small routine numerical gain.
